two aspects: (i) the effect of learned prior in variational inference, and (ii) the performance of ß-VAEs with RealNVP prior.

, using powerful prior can help to improve the variatinal lower-bound, even with a single latent variable.
, using a powerful posterior and a learned prior is an effective way to improve VAE, especially when the posterior is Gaussian.
, using learned RealN-VP prior and Gaussian posteriors, VAE can be as effective as hierarchical VAEs, and can be used to improve the rate-distortion curve of ß-VAEs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when coupled together, learned prior and Gaussian posteriors may have a better chance of achieving good performance than either alone.
using powerful posterior distribution and learned prior can be a simple yet effective approach to improve VAE.
we propose using learned prior to improve variational inference, and we show that, with just one latent variable and RealNVP prior in VAE, the test NLL can be as good as deep hierarchical VAEs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of prior is important and using a more expressive prior may be a more effective way to improve the lower-bound than using a hierarchical structure.

, with appropriate prior, we can use a simple VAE with one or two latent variables to achieve comparable test NLL to very deep hierarchical VAEs, and we can also use learned prior to improve the ß-VAEs.
